title: Beginner Aerial Sling (short) Dance Follow Along | aerial practice

observation_window.sampling: provider default; not continuous motion capture

extraction.teacher_style: The instructor provides calm, step-by-step breakdowns of aerial sling tricks with on-screen text reinforcing spoken directions. She encourages beginners by relating routines to past struggles and reviewing sequences from the top.

lesson_structure.note: Welcome and introduction to aerial sling flow
Breaking down trick 1: inverted L shape
Breaking down trick 2: sitting position from inversion

common_mistakes: Climbing up looking uncleaned if legs muscle not engaged
safety: Be prepared for slight discomfort if this is your first time having silks wrap around your thighs

steps_taught.name: Inverted L-shape
steps_taught.description: Lean down, bring knees up and straighten legs into inverted L

steps_taught.name: Sitting position
steps_taught.description: Bring feet inside silks, reach silks, and push hip up

steps_taught.name: Hip lock
steps_taught.description: Reach clockwise, swing left leg to draw a circle into hip lock

what_works: Clear on-screen text matching spoken instructions
Repetition of tricks from the top
what_hinders: Fast transitions in aerial work can be hard to follow without previous experience

quotes.text: Today you are going to learn this simple beginner flow.
Be prepared for slight discomfort if this is your first time.
Two tips to remember throughout your practice.

evidence_segments.observation: Instructor stands beside hanging silk hammock, demonstrating alignment before going into inversion
Instructor positions in hammock in side profile showing thigh wrap placement

extraction.distinctive_method: Breaking down a continuous aerial flow into numbered distinct tricks (1-6) with dedicated practice segments for each.
